S022.title: The ribbon cutting table
S022.bridge: When a gold piece measuring 6 cm is left on the cutting table, pause. Which earlier whole can you reconstruct from four copies of that piece?

S023.title: The four signal flags
S023.bridge: When the harbourmaster crosses out the rows with A beside B and the rows with C beside D, find a signal crossed out twice. How many orders can the two clips make?

S025.title: The print shop discount wheel
S025.bridge: Pause when the price tag turns from $80 to $100. To undo the $20 rise, which price belongs under the fraction bar on the sale sticker?

S026.title: The bird hide tally rail
S026.bridge: Put a finger on each end of the bird hide’s two observation brackets. Which tally gets included a second time when you add their totals?

S027.title: Two shelves in the pottery kiln
S027.bridge: At the kiln, four pale pieces have one dot and four dark pieces have three dots. What happens to the number of dots when you exchange one group of four?

revisits.233: At the cutting table, one quarter of the original ribbon becomes red and one third of the remainder becomes blue. Why can the red and blue strips have equal lengths?
revisits.297: When the potter imagines forty pale pieces, how many dots does that predict? Watch what happens to the dot total when one four-piece group changes clay.
revisits.314: When the tag for period four turns over, the hide still has six observation periods. What total can you reconstruct from their mean before looking at the two shorter brackets?
revisits.324: In the gold ribbon puzzle, start at the last cut and reconstruct the blue-and-gold piece. If a gift were added between two cuts, at which point in your backward steps would you take it out?
revisits.347: When the print shop marks its framed print down, which price now represents one hundred percent? Check the tempting twenty-five-percent sticker against the target price.
revisits.353: Clip the two forbidden flag pairs at the same time. Which rows receive two crossings? In your later arrangement, check whether the two forbidden pairs share a letter.
